item.title: [7.3] Japan government bond yields fall as global markets steady
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Japanese government bond yields saw a significant drop on Friday, as the 10-year yield fell to levels not recorded since mid-September. Global bond markets stabilizing and shifts in central bank policies played a key role in this decline. Even though the Bank of Japan raised rates recently, inflation in Tokyo is rising, fueling predictions of additional rate hikes.

WHY IT MATTERS

The significant drop in Japanese bond yields amidst expectations of further BoJ rate hikes signals important cross-currents in global fixed income markets that macro investors should monitor.

item.title: [7.1] Global Market: Eurozone bonds face pressure as energy shock fuels rate hike bets
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Eurozone bond yields rose sharply as energy-driven inflation strengthened expectations of further ECB rate hikes through 2027. French yields hit an 18-year high, while spreads for French and Italian debt widened amid fiscal concerns. Investors are reassessing inflation, borrowing costs, debt sustainability and political risks across heavily indebted eurozone economies.

WHY IT MATTERS

The spike in eurozone bond yields and widening spreads signal growing fiscal and inflation stress that matters for global market sentiment.

item.title: [6.7] Global Market: European shares slide as surging bond yields hit risk appetite
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

European shares opened the final quarter lower as elevated global bond yields and persistent inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment. Higher energy costs and expectations of prolonged interest rates pressured equities, while softer oil prices offered limited relief to markets.

WHY IT MATTERS

The shift in European equities driven by surging bond yields and persistent inflation marks an important macro trend for the start of the quarter, though it builds on existing monetary policy themes.
